open.speaker: hollis
lines: Jerky's two dollars, coffee's free with jerky, and I don't do directions. Everybody wants directions.
...You ain't lost, are you. You're the ones. Marlene's people.
CB's on 19 and the squelch is wide open. He's listening to static on purpose.

passives.line: The CB's clock reads 2:10 and it's past noon. He's set it to the only time he cares about.
The logbook under the counter has a pencil in it worn to nothing. He writes in it every night.
He says 'ain't lost' like he was once. Like he's been lost on this road since he was nine.

static.line: He's watching the clock, not you. Ask him what happens at ten past two and watch what his hands do.

options.text: Squelch is wide open. You're not listening for truckers.
We don't want directions. We want your logbook.

buy.speaker: hollis
lines: Six dollars. Deer, not beef. Don't tell the health man.
...Huh. Most folks talk me down. You just paid. I'll remember that.

squelch.speaker: hollis
lines: Truckers don't come down 62 no more. Not since the bridge.
I'm listening for ten past two. Something comes on every band at ten past two, and I've heard it since I was nine on my daddy's set.
Every band. That's not a transmitter. A transmitter has a band.

squelch_fail.speaker: hollis
lines: I listen to what I listen to. It's my set.
You want radio, Orville up on the Heights has a tower. Go bother Orville.

logbook_hard.speaker: hollis
lines: You want nothing of mine. Get your jerky or get on.
(He puts a hand flat on the counter, over the book.)
Well. Now we know where the book is.

hub.speaker: hollis
hub.prompt: Hollis keeps a hand near the book.

options.text: A man ought to keep times. Show us the times.
The two men in the sedan. They told us you'd cooperate.
We've got it on tape. Three notes, strongest in igloo 7.
(Sit at the counter and listen to the static with him.)

times.speaker: hollis
lines: (He opens the book.) Ten past two. Ten past two. Ten past two. Eleven, that was once, in '89, and I'd had a beer.
Two lights, red, over the TNT ridge, moving against the wind. Six years of nights. You're the first to look.
Six years of the same minute. Either he's right or his clock's wrong, and I'd like to check the clock.

times_fail.speaker: hollis
lines: It's a private book. A man's times are his own.
Carl Ridge keeps his in his head. Go ask Carl what time it stands up.

sedan.speaker: hollis
lines: Never said a word to me. Sat in that car two nights, engine off, never came in for coffee. I wrote the plates. There weren't none.
Monday and Tuesday. Watched the chapel roof like Carl. Left at ten past two both nights, same as the lights.
They leave when it leaves. They're not watching the roof. They're watching the clock.

sedan_fail.speaker: hollis
lines: They never told you nothing, 'cause they never talk. And now I know you're a liar.
Jerky's four dollars for liars. Get on.

passives.line: You borrowed the suits' credit and it bounced. The bell on his door sounds like a cash drawer shutting.

tape.speaker: hollis
lines: (He listens with his eyes shut.) That's it. That's it. Igloo 7.
I was nine. Daddy's set, the night the two couples came in off 62. Three notes, carrier dropped, Daddy pulled the plug, it kept going.
I've never told nobody that. The unplugged part.
Lonnie at the pawn said the same thing. Unplugged. That's two sets and no power.

listen.speaker: hollis
lines: (The static rises and falls. At some point he pours you a coffee you didn't pay for.)
Ten past two's a long way off. You can come back. Most don't.
He means it. He's counting on it, a little.
